content.text:
The drawing is acridine with a dimethylamino group on each outer ring, which makes it acridine orange (3,6-bis(dimethylamino)acridine).

**Ring system.** The central ring contains the ring nitrogen N at the top and a CH at the bottom. The two outer benzene rings are fused on either side of it.

**Substituents.** Each outer ring carries an N(CH3)2 group at the position meta to the ring fusion carbon bonded to N. That is the 3 and 6 position pattern of acridine.

**SMILES construction.** Starting from one dimethylamino group, I wrote the left ring, then the central ring through the ring nitrogen, then the right ring:

CN(C)c1ccc2cc3ccc(N(C)C)cc3nc2c1

**Atom check.**
- Left ring: c1 (carrying NMe2), c, c, c2 (fusion carbon bonded to the central CH), then the central CH, then c3 (fusion carbon of the right ring).
- Right ring: c3, c, c, c(NMe2), c, c3 (fusion carbon bonded to N), then n, then c2 (left-ring fusion carbon bonded to N), then c1 (the left-ring CH between the NMe2-bearing carbon and that fusion carbon).
- The left NMe2 carbon sits two atoms from the fusion carbon bonded to N, which matches the drawing, and the right side is symmetric.
- All ring closures are paired and the aromatic atoms are consistent.

SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc2cc3ccc(N(C)C)cc3nc2c1
